It publishes the agrifood-systems lens (16.5 Gt, 31.73%) on that same total, with FAO-published shares, sector shares of each gas (food is 59.7% of methane and 80.7% of nitrous oxide) and per-capita values in EM. candidates.caveats: (1) LICENCE CHAIN. FAO's documentation cites the wrong PRIMAP-hist version. The GT note (release October 2023) says Energy, IPPU, Waste and Other 'are sourced from the PRIMAP-hist v2.4 dataset'. Brief 115 (2025) says 'PRIMAP-hist dataset v2.4' and cites v2.4.2 with DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10705513, which resolves to v2.5.1. But the 2023 values in GT match PRIMAP-hist v2.7 HISTTP, not v2.6.1. Germany Energy CO2 2021/2022/2023: GT 625,000 / 618,000 / 550,000 kt; v2.7 HISTTP 625000 / 618000 / 550000; v2.6.1 HISTTP 626000 / 616000 / 558000. USA IPPU CO2: GT 134,000 / 139,000 / 137,000; v2.7 HISTTP the same; v2.6.1 131000 / 136000 / 135000. Germany IPPU CH4 2022/2023: GT 8.96 / 8.51; v2.7 the same; v2.6.1 8.93 / 8.4. PRIMAP-hist v2.7 is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and its TP series has no commercial licence. Following the jones-2025-national-contributions precedent (a downstream CC BY label cannot lift upstream NC-SA), the non-AFOLU items, the All-sectors totals and every EM share or per-capita value that uses them should be classed noncommercial, with downloads under BY-NC-SA and PRIMAP-hist credited. This also affects the already published food.faostat.agrifood-emissions-world.share, whose denominator is item 6825, while the faostat source is classed open. Pre- and post-production estimates also 'integrate emission information from the PRIMAP-hist dataset' (GT note), so the agrifood numerator may carry the same chain. I could not test this, and it is worth asking FAO (faostat@fao.org / copyright@fao.org). Registering a separate source entry (e.g. FAOSTAT all-sector emissions, class noncommercial, quoting both terms) is cleaner than changing the open faostat entry. (2) Further upstream: PRIMAP-hist TP energy CO2 uses CDIAC, extended with Energy Institute growth rates. EDGAR 2024 is used for other sectors and gases 'except energy CO2', so IEA-EDGAR CO2 does not enter the energy CO2. The International bunkers item (EDGAR v6.0) is outside the total and should not be used. (3) PRIMAP-hist itself says the TP scenario 'is no longer actively maintained' (v2.8 description), and FAO keeps using it. (4) LULUCF here is FAO's net, inventory-style number (net forest conversion minus the Forestland sink plus organic soils and fires). It is 0.47 Gt in 2023, negative in some years (World 2013: −0.19 Gt) and strongly negative for China (−0.83 Gt), the USA (−0.34 Gt) and India (−0.15 Gt). GCB's land-use-change CO2 is a bookkeeping estimate of 4.75 Gt CO2 in 2023. The two must never be mixed, and the stacked chart needs a band that can go below zero. (5) GWP is AR5 (CH4 28, N2O 265), the same as EDGAR. IGCC and IPCC AR6 use AR6 values. (6) Non-AFOLU values are rounded to 3 significant figures (PRIMAP 'final'). (7) 29 territories have AFOLU-only 'All sectors' totals. Country rankings must use only areas that have all six IPCC items, and say 'No data for energy in FAOSTAT' for the rest. (8) EM shares use the with-LULUCF total as denominator, so a country with a net sink shows 'All sectors without LULUCF' above 100% (USA 105.94%). (9) FAO's 2026 release (data to 2024) is due in October 2026. The PRIMAP version must be re-checked at that release (v2.8 is also CC BY-NC-SA).

research.recommendation:
Use FAOSTAT as the single basis for 'all greenhouse gases → by sector → by gas → by country / per person'. Use Emissions totals (GT, already cached) for the kilotonne values and the sector and gas stacks. Add a new artifact, Emissions indicators (EM, bulks-faostat …/Climate_change_Emissions_indicators_E_All_Data_(Normalized).zip, 4,655,416 bytes), for FAO's own shares and per-capita values. It is the only producer dataset that puts the six non-overlapping IPCC sectors (Energy 38.79, Industry 4.43, Agriculture 6.24, Waste 1.98, Other 0.20, Land use 0.47 Gt CO2e; total 52.11 Gt, 2023, AR5 GWP100, including LULUCF) and the agrifood-system lens (16.54 Gt = 31.73%) on one denominator. FAO publishes the 31.73% itself in EM (item 6518, element 726313), so the existing food.faostat.agrifood-emissions-world.share can be taken as published instead of computed. Food must not be drawn as a seventh band. It overlaps Energy (on-farm energy, processing, transport, household), IPPU (fertiliser, retail F-gases), Waste and LULUCF, and FAO publishes no 'rest of economy' remainder. The sector node should therefore show the six IPCC bands and drill from 'Agriculture' and 'Land use' to a 'Food system' node that stacks Farm gate + Land-use change + Pre- and post-production (exactly 16.54 Gt). Its sentence should say that food's emissions run across the sectors and make up 31.7% of the total.

LICENCE ACTION BEFORE ANY CODE. Comparing the values shows that GT's Energy, IPPU, Waste and Other items in the October 2025 release are PRIMAP-hist v2.7 HISTTP (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), not v2.4 as FAO's documents state. Register them, the All-sectors totals and the EM shares and per-capita values built on them as class noncommercial (e.g. a separate source entry for FAOSTAT all-sector emissions, quoting the FAO terms and the PRIMAP-hist v2.7 licence, crediting both). Note that the already published food.faostat.agrifood-emissions-world.share (denominator item 6825) currently sits under the open faostat entry and should move with them. Ask FAO which PRIMAP version and terms apply, including whether pre- and post-production uses PRIMAP. Re-check at FAO's October 2026 release, which will probably use v2.8, also NC-SA. Noncommercial is allowed in dashboard nodes, so this changes download terms, not feasibility.

How this relates to the CO2-only GCB numbers. GCB/GCP stay the CO2 detail one level down: fossil by fuel and country, per capita, consumption versus territorial. The bridge is IGCC-2025 (registered, CC BY 4.0), whose world by-gas series uses exactly GCB's CO2 (CO2_FFI 2024 38.5986 = GCP 38,598.578 Mt; CO2_LULUCF 2023 4.7456 = GCB land-use change) plus EDGAR non-CO2 (CC BY), totalling 56.8 Gt CO2e in 2024 (AR6 GWP). The chapter can go: FAOSTAT all-GHG total → FAOSTAT sectors (food node across them) → FAOSTAT by gas (CO2 38.27, CH4 9.43, N2O 2.95, F-gases 1.45 = 52.11) → the CO2 band opens the existing GCB/GCP fossil-by-fuel view. An optional IGCC node can show 'fossil CO2 versus land-use CO2 versus other gases' on GCB's own CO2. Each view must state its basis, and FAOSTAT and IGCC/GCB values must never be combined or subtracted. The two bases differ for documented reasons. FAOSTAT is AR5 and IGCC AR6. FAOSTAT's land use is a net inventory-style figure (0.47 Gt CO2e, of which CO2 0.24 Gt, with the forest sink netted in), while GCB's land-use change is bookkeeping (4.75 Gt CO2, 2023). FAOSTAT excludes international bunkers; GCB's global fossil total includes them.

Owner's label points. 'Where food emissions come from' should be split into 'by stage' (farm gate / land-use change / pre- and post-production, from GT) and 'by country'. A per-food view would come from FAOSTAT's livestock (GLE, registered) and crops (GCE) domains, which is outside this need. Per-person labels should read 'average per person in each country (national emissions ÷ population)', using EM's published 'Emissions per capita' (World 6.44 t CO2e, 2023). For individual-level carbon, the existing SEI income-group shares are the lens to point to.

research.recommendation:
Build Need B entirely from FAOSTAT, under the existing faostat source (CC BY 4.0, open). Only one new artifact is needed.

1. Stage and process (part 1). Use the already-cached GT file (faostat/emissions-totals). Publish 22 non-overlapping process items (Element 723113, FAO TIER 1, 1990–2023, world and every country) grouped into FAO's three stages: Farm gate, Land-use change, Pre- and post-production. They add exactly to the published Agrifood systems total (16,535,072 kt for World 2023, checked to under 0.1 kt for several years and countries). Never stack the overlapping aggregates (Emissions from livestock, Emissions from crops, Emissions on agricultural land, IPCC Agriculture, AFOLU, LULUCF). Keep Forestland, the -3.6 Gt sink, out of the stack.

2. Food product (part 2). Register the Emissions intensities (EI) bulk zip as a new artifact (faostat/emissions-intensities, https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/Environment_Emissions_intensities_E_All_Data_(Normalized).zip, DateUpdate 2026-02-20). Publish 'Emissions (CO2eq) (AR5)' and 'Emissions intensity' for its 14 commodities, 1961–2023, world and countries. It is the only open, producer-published, per-product time series. Every label must say it is on-the-farm emissions only (FAO: not comparable with life-cycle figures). Show these as ranked bars, never as a stack, because the 14 do not partition a published total. Rank countries by commodity emissions rather than intensity, because country intensities can be extreme (Ethiopia beef 184 kg CO2eq/kg).

3. Animals. Use the cached GLE file. Replace the single-band livestock methane node with a stack of 16 non-overlapping species in Mt CH4. They add exactly to the published All Animals value (115.2 Mt, 2023). Do not convert to CO2eq ourselves.

4. Later and optional. Register the GLEAM 3 dashboard (manual acquisition, class noncommercial until FAO resolves the CC BY 4.0 vs CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 conflict) for one 2015 life-cycle view of livestock products by source (feed, land-use change, enteric, manure, energy, post-farm). Register SU-EATABLE LIFE (CC BY 4.0) as an open per-kg life-cycle list to sit beside the display-only Poore & Nemecek values. Leave GPP until the October 2026 GT release brings the vintages back in line.

Registry work before any code (AGENTS.md rule 5): add the EI artifact and description to pipeline/sources/faostat.yaml, cite the EI methodological note https://files-faostat.fao.org/production/EI/EI_e.pdf, and update docs/sources.md if GLEAM or SEL are added.

Labels that answer the owner's feedback: the country ranking should say 'Which countries' food systems emit the most', and the new entry should say 'Where food's emissions come from' (stages, then processes, then foods).

For the emissions chapter's 'where emissions come from' pages, add a card that leads into the food chapter. Its share must be shown as FAO's own (agrifood 31.7% of FAO's all-sector total including land use, 2023), because those pages are CO2-only (GCB). Never add FAO's CO2eq into the GCB CO2 stacks.

research.recommendation:
No openly licensed producer publishes a world-average footprint per person split by consumption category, or tonnes per person by global income group. WID.world, which holds the income-group series, has been a parked domain since about 29 September 2026, and no data licence is readable anywhere. The other sources that have these figures are display-only (Hot or Cool, Sitra/IGES, IPCC, UNEP) or not open access (Ivanova 2016, Chancel 2022). Do not compute either one from SEI shares, EXIOBASE or GCB totals.

What can be built honestly:
(a) Register Naturvårdsverket's per-person consumption footprint (Sweden, 2008-2023, open). It is the one dataset found where the producer itself publishes 'a person's footprint by what they consume', in t CO2e per person. The six non-overlapping parts add to the total (7.62 t in 2023).
(b) Register Defra's UK carbon footprint (OGL v3). It publishes 10.2 t CO2e per person (2023) and the full 699.2 Mt split into 14 non-overlapping end-use categories, including 'Food and beverages' 74.7 Mt and 'Transportation' 150.4 Mt. It also has a 34-category COICOP household time series 1990-2023.
(c) Optionally, register the JRC Consumption Footprint (COM_REUSE / CC BY 4.0). Eurostat's per-inhabitant total for EU27 and member states can come automatically; the area breakdown needs a manual download and a check of its units. Label it a bottom-up LCA that is not comparable with input-output footprints.
(d) For consumption per person by country with a world value, OECD GHGFP 2025 (FD_GHG T_CO2E_PS; world 6.0 t in 2022) is the only direct publication found. A person must first read the OECD terms and the dataset note (oecd.org is 403 to scripts), because the methodology uses IEA data excluded as third-party material. Until then, keep the GCB consumption totals node as it is and do not divide it by population.
(e) Relabel the existing nodes so they say what they are: 'Average fossil CO2 per person, by country (territorial)' for emissions.gcp-2025.fossil-co2-per-capita, and 'Share of world CO2 by income group' for the SEI node, with no 'per person' wording.
(f) Fix the SEI node's latest year. SEI's 2023 national values are territorial while 1990-2022 are consumption-based (CHE 122.0 to 32.7 Mt, USA 5,643 to 4,911 Mt). Show 2022 as the latest consumption-based year, or flag 2023 as a different basis. Add this to docs/sources.md and the sei-emissions-inequality status note.
(g) The food gap the owner raised can be closed from (a) and (b), whose food bands are producer-published ('Livsmedel' 1.35 t per person in Sweden 2023; UK 'Food and beverages' 74.7 Mt). Each food band should link to the FAOSTAT agrifood node (31.7% of global GHG including LULUCF), with the different bases stated: consumption footprint vs. FAOSTAT's production-side agrifood total.

The kit orders bands by their first year of data, so a 1961 start would draw 8 bands with no published total and then a jump in 1990 when 14 more bands begin. The claim 'a stacked chart has no gaps to fill' is wrong for some countries. 13 area-item series between 1990 and 2023 have internal holes: Synthetic Fertilizers in Bahamas (22 of 34 years), Bermuda (22), Botswana (27) and Congo (32), Crop Residues in Hong Kong (27), and others. FAO's total still equals the sum of the rows present. However, the kit's rule that 'nothing is ever stacked on a gap' needs to handle a band that disappears mid-series. Check it before building.
There are 7 small negative process values, for example Somalia Synthetic Fertilizers: -0.0265 (2004) to -0.689 (2011) kt. A stack must handle a negative band without inventing a zero.

Country rankings must not list both 'China' (Area 351, 2,316,750 kt in 2023) and 'China, mainland' (41, 2,265,846 kt). Area 351 is the sum of mainland, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan. The researcher checked 'China' and 'China, mainland' as if both were countries.

verification.overall:
All three candidates hold up on licence. Naturvårdsverket/SCB is open (Naturvårdsverket's 'Öppna data får användas fritt' plus SCB's CC0), Defra is OGL 3.0 (stated on the dataset's cover sheet, AR5 GWP, no IEA or third-party exclusion in the methods) and JRC is COM_REUSE / CC BY 4.0. None gives the world-average 'personal footprint by category' the owner expected. I did not re-test the researcher's negative claims (WID parked, Hot or Cool and others display-only, OECD 403).

(1) Naturvårdsverket is adopt-with-changes. It is the only producer-published per-person split by consumption area. The parts add to Totalt only within ±0.01 t (exact in 11 of 16 years; 2023 is exact at 7.62). Its 'Övrigt' (0.98 t) cannot be rebuilt from SCB groups (about 0.94 t), so cite Naturvårdsverket as publisher and SCB as the responsible authority. The GWP basis is unclear: the page shows an AR4 table. Separate household (4.70 t) from public consumption plus investment (2.92 t) before calling any of it 'personal'. Snapshot the HTML payload, and expect the 2024 vintage in autumn 2026.

(2) Defra is adopt. Every additivity claim re-derived exactly from the raw ODS (sha256 matches a2fa54f9…085b): 14 end-use parts = 699,201.9 kt; 34 COICOP = 528,626.1 = households 406,969.1 + direct 121,657.0; Food 71,054.6 + non-alcoholic beverages 3,677.2 = Food and beverages 74,731.8. One label correction: 'Recreation and communication', not 'Recreation'. Per-person exists only as a total (10.2034 t).

(3) JRC is adopt-with-changes and limited to Eurostat's per-inhabitant total (EU27 2024 7.64 t, verified). The area breakdown is unverified (JSF manual download) and runs only to 2021, so it cannot be stacked under the 2024 total. Take the licence class from JRC's COM_REUSE record, not from Eurostat, whose notice makes third-party-sourced data non-commercial. Label it as an LCA of household products only.

For the food gap, Sweden's 'Livsmedel' (1.35 t per person) and the UK's 'Food and beverages' (74.7 Mt) are both producer-published. They are consumption-side and exclude restaurants (UK 36.7 Mt), so link them to FAOSTAT's production-side 31.7% with the bases stated, never as equivalents.
